The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Crypto's 'casino-chips' are disappearing, adding to pain from spot ETF outflows. Your day-ahead look for Nov. 17, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ex-OpenAI researcher fund dumps bitcoin miners, cuts IREN 94% after portfolio slump. The fund swapped its common stock in Bloom Energy, Nebius and SanDisk for call options, keeping its bet on AI power, computing and memory. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin remains penned in near $64,000 even as ETF outflow streak ends. Bitcoin (BTC) is down a further 1.0% since midnight UTC at around $64,200, with its bounce from the weekend selloff stalled and pressure building on all fronts. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Solana Foundation takes majority stake in crypto data provider CoinGecko. The foundation plans Solana-powered trading on CoinGecko's website, GeckoTerminal and app. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

New DeFi-yield generation targets ‘scam-like’ bank accounts that keep all the interest. Crypto native firms like Animoca Brands are betting AI-based agentic commerce to style every area of finance with the so-called “DeFi mullet” Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Fed Governor Michael Barr warns AI agents could trigger bank runs in minutes. In a speech at an AI event in Italy, Barr said automated financial decisions could overwhelm banks and raises concerns about AI systems bypassing security controls. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $64,782 with a +1.30% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,811.92 with a +1.07% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.title: 2025 Crypto Regulatory Round-Up
items.description:
What is the GENIUS Act and how does it regulate stablecoins?

The GENIUS Act is United States legislation passed in 2025 that establishes a federal regulatory framework for stablecoin issuers. It mandates strict requirements for reserve backing, audits, and financial integrity. The law also places restrictions on the domestic offering of foreign issued stablecoins, prompting a global acceleration in stablecoin policy development. [...] National regulators that have not yet developed or implemented stablecoin regulation will continue to make progress. By July 2026, U.S. federal and state regulators are required to promulgate final regulations to implement the GENIUS Act. This will include processes to license and regulate federal stablecoin issuers, and establishing criteria that foreign stablecoin issuers must meet in order to offer their stablecoins in the U.S. In Singapore, draft legislation to implement a stablecoin regime [...] We’re beginning to see regulation reconfigure usage patterns in the global stablecoin market, and that will increase over time. Europe has seen a rotation toward MiCA-compliant stablecoins as CASPs have been generally restricted from offering non-compliant ones. In the United States, the GENIUS Act places restrictions on the domestic offering of foreign-issued stablecoins.
